title: Unsupervised prototype transfer: problem, decisions and plan
subtitle: Planning page. Analysis numbers below are generated from outputs/results/*.json by scripts/build_plan_data.py; the text on this page is edited by hand in dashboard/plan_content.json.

problem.statement: Adapt an interpretable bird-sound ProtoPNet (AudioProtoPNet, pretrained on focal Xeno-Canto clips) to field soundscapes without using any soundscape labels, so that each prototype keeps detecting its own species there.
given: Pretrained AudioProtoPNet-5-BirdSet-XCL (XCL is focal Xeno-Canto data only; HSN soundscapes are a BirdSet test set, so neither their audio nor labels were in pretraining).
Labeled focal clips for the 21 HSN species (focal train split).
Unlabeled audio of the soundscape train split (60 sites, 7,200 clips).
forbidden: Soundscape labels in any loss term.
Soundscape labels for checkpoint selection or hyperparameter tuning.
Soundscape test sites in any training or adaptation step.
goal: Soundscape macro AUC and prevalence-honest AP move toward the soundscape-only oracle.
Most prototypes keep their detection AUC from focal to soundscape (small |Δ_k|), not just on average.
Top soundscape matches are the species' call, not noise-floor energy or another bird.
problem.transferable: Prototype k of species c is transferable if (1) its detection AUC for c on soundscapes is close to its focal AUC (Δ_k ≈ 0), (2) its top soundscape matches are c's call rather than wind-band noise or a co-occurring species, and (3) the class-level soundscape score does not pay for it. A monotone rescaling of activations is allowed: shrinkage with preserved ranking is a calibration shift, not a failure.

shift_factors.name: Lower SNR and different background
shift_factors.evidence: Median positive activation falls to 39% of the focal value (0.27 → 0.10) while ranking mostly survives (median prototype AUC 0.87).
shift_factors.label_free_fix: Mix real soundscape background into focal clips at random SNR.

shift_factors.name: Overlapping species
shift_factors.evidence: A median of 85% of each prototype's top-20 soundscape false matches contain another annotated species (44% base rate).
shift_factors.label_free_fix: Overlay a focal clip of species B on one of species A with the multi-label target {A, B}. The labels are correct and need no soundscape labels.

shift_factors.name: Noise-only clips outside the focal support
shift_factors.evidence: 54% of soundscape train clips contain no target species. 5 prototypes that fire above 1 kHz on focal peak near 0.1 kHz (wind) on soundscapes.
shift_factors.label_free_fix: Use low-confidence soundscape clips as background; flag prototypes whose unlabeled-soundscape peak frequency drifts.

decisions.title: Unsupervised protocol
decisions.choice: Zero soundscape labels in the loss, in checkpoint selection and in tuning. Soundscape labels are used only for final evaluation (and for clearly marked diagnostics).
decisions.why: This is the realistic deployment: audio is cheap, annotation is the bottleneck.

decisions.title: Inductive setting
decisions.choice: Adapt on audio from the 60 train sites; evaluate on the 30 unseen test sites.
decisions.why: Follows from the site split; avoids touching test audio. A transductive variant can be an extra.

decisions.title: Splits
decisions.choice: Keep the current splits: focal grouped by recordist, soundscape grouped by site.
decisions.why: Both groupings stop near-duplicate audio crossing train and test.

decisions.title: Focal test and val
decisions.choice: Focal val is used for checkpoint selection (as in train_protopnet.py); focal test is a retention reference only, not a generalization score.
decisions.why: Focal clips are Xeno-Canto, so they are very likely part of XCL's training data. Soundscape test is the only clean held-out number.

decisions.choice: The existing focal-only run is a valid source-only baseline: it selects on focal val only; soundscape val is just logged.
decisions.why: Checked in scripts/train_protopnet.py. No rerun needed.

decisions.choice: Shift-matched augmentation (background mixing + overlap mixing) while fine-tuning from pretrained.

decisions.title: Headline metric
decisions.choice: Soundscape macro AP on the primary species. Macro AUC, cmAP over the 12 and focal retention are secondary.

decisions.title: Canonical evaluation
decisions.choice: One script, scripts/canonical_eval.py, scores every model on the same test clips (checked) and writes outputs/results/canonical_eval.json. No model is reported from any other script.
decisions.why: Makes every comparison, including future runs, use identical species sets, metrics, CIs and criteria.

decisions.title: Prototype delta definition
decisions.choice: Report both: Δ (soundscape negatives = all other soundscape clips, as before) and Δ on matched negatives (soundscape negatives = clips with another target species).
decisions.why: Focal negatives are other species' clips, so matched negatives compare like with like. They also remove easy empty-background negatives. On the pretrained model 42 of 60 prototypes fail on matched negatives against 26 with the old definition.

decisions.title: Label-budget curve
decisions.choice: Add it as Stage 2b: soundscape-only models trained with 100 to 7,200 labeled clips under one fixed schedule, 3 seeds each.
decisions.why: Separates a data gap (labels needed) from a methodology gap (how to get that information without labels) and gives label-free methods a label-equivalence yardstick.

decisions.title: Deliverable
decisions.choice: A method, plus the analysis of how and why prototypes fail to transfer, plus strong baselines (pretrained, focal-only, soundscape-only oracle, label-budget curve).
decisions.why: Confirmed by you. The analysis and baselines stand on their own even if the method closes only part of the gap.

decisions.title: Dev set (separate from test)
decisions.choice: Dev = the 10 val sites plus 10 sites carved from train (20 labeled sites), held out from adaptation. Val stops being a separate set. Dev labels never enter the training loss.
decisions.why: The Stage 2 gate and its follow-ups used test labels, and soundscape val (10 sites, 9 of 21 species with no positives) is too small to decide with. Dev only costs data during development: finalists are refit on all 70 non-test sites.

where.note: --split dev|test, recording which split was scored

decisions.title: Test-set use rule
decisions.choice: Test is scored only by scripts/canonical_eval.py, for frozen finalists, once each. Every decision and diagnostic uses dev, or all 70 non-test sites for diagnostics that fit nothing. canonical_eval records which split it scored.
decisions.why: The Stage 2 decisions already looked at test; this keeps the final numbers clean.

where.note: --split dev|test and a split field in the JSON

decisions.title: Tiered evaluation protocol
decisions.choice: 1) Diagnostics that fit nothing: pool labels of all 70 non-test sites. 2) Screening trained ideas: the 20-site dev split, seed 0. 3) Finalists (2 or 3): 3-fold site-grouped cross-validation over the 70 non-test sites, then refit on all 70 and score test once.
decisions.why: Site heterogeneity makes a single small dev set noisy, but cross-validating every run triples the cost, so it is kept for the end.

stages.title: Diagnostics without training
what: 2.0 Extract pretrained responses on soundscape-train (GPU inference). This gives each clip's maximum species probability: the label-free background manifest (lowest 30%) for R1b and the teacher soft labels for R4.
2.1 Corrupt focal test clips with soundscape background at SNR 20/10/5/0/-5 dB, with an overlaid second species, and with both; compute Δ_k(synthetic) for the pretrained model.
2.2 From unlabeled soundscape-train audio compute per-prototype fire rate, peak-frequency shift and activation quantiles; correlate with the real Δ_k.
2.3 Inference-only baselines: re-estimated input normalization; zero the weights of prototypes flagged by 2.2.
stages.verify: Spearman(Δ_k synthetic, Δ_k real) over the 60 prototypes.
stages.gate: Proceed to augmentation training only if the correlation is above 0.5 for at least one corruption. Otherwise switch to adaptation on real soundscape features.
stages.result: Run 1 (job 11787583): the extraction reproduces the committed pretrained numbers. The gate FAILED: no corruption reproduces which prototypes fail (Spearman between −0.20 and +0.10, all CIs include 0), the synthetic activation ratio stays at 0.91–0.97 against 0.30 real, and no label-free predictor works (|ρ| ≤ 0.15). The label-free background selector works (97% of selected clips are empty). Follow-up (job 11809428, queued) tests random focal windows and quieter-bird mixing down to −25 dB.

recipe.intro: Stage 3 is a ladder: every run changes one thing relative to the run before it, so each gain or loss can be attributed. All runs start from the pretrained model and reuse scripts/train_protopnet.py. Every new flag defaults to off, so the existing focal-only and soundscape-only runs stay reproducible.
inherited: Pretrained XCL sliced to the 21 HSN species (105 prototypes), as build_hsn_protopnet() does.
warm 2 epochs (prototypes + last layer, backbone frozen) → joint 12 epochs → push onto focal-train positives → last layer 4 epochs.
AdamW with OneCycle. Warm lr 1e-3 (prototypes, last). Joint lr: backbone 2e-5, prototypes 1e-4, last 1e-4. Last-layer lr 1e-3. Weight decay 1e-4.
The model's asymmetric multi-label loss + 0.01 × orthogonality. Batch size 32, bf16 autocast.
Random gain ±6 dB, 2 time masks (up to 60 frames), 2 frequency masks (up to 24 bins).
Best joint and last epoch by focal val cmAP. Never uses soundscape labels.
Seed 0 to screen every run; the finalists are rerun with seeds 0, 1, 2 and reported as mean ± sd plus the site-bootstrap CI.
From history.json, the earlier focal-only run took about 13 min and soundscape-only about 23 min end to end, so the whole ladder is a few GPU-hours.
recipe.observation: Why checkpoint selection needs care: in the focal-only run, soundscape val cmAP is highest at the first joint epoch (0.608) and decays to 0.575 while focal val cmAP rises from 0.951 to 0.972. Selecting on focal val therefore tends to pick epochs with worse transfer. This curve comes from monitoring data, not from selection, so any epoch budget we choose because of it is reported as a recipe choice, not tuned on soundscape labels.

ladder.name: anchored-focal
ladder.change: Joint phase skipped (--joint-epochs 0): backbone frozen, only prototypes and last layer train; then push and last layer.
ladder.isolates: Is the focal-only drop caused by forgetting in the backbone?
ladder.evidence: Direct, ours: the 34 fine prototypes lose 0.907 → 0.850 AUC; the soundscape val curve above.

ladder.name: bg-generic
ladder.change: Background mixing with generic coloured noise (pink, brown, white).
ladder.evidence: Literature: BirdSet's own recipe mixes soundscape-like noise (p = 0.5) to bridge focal to soundscape.

ladder.name: bg-target
ladder.change: Same as R1a, but backgrounds are real HSN soundscape-train clips that the pretrained model scores as empty.
ladder.isolates: Does target-domain background beat generic noise? This is the new claim.
ladder.evidence: Hypothesis. Indirect support only (target-location pseudo-labeling helps in BirdCLEF).

ladder.name: overlap
ladder.change: Multi-label mixup: overlay a second focal species with the union of both labels.
ladder.isolates: Does teaching overlap reduce cross-species false matches?
ladder.evidence: Ours: a median of 85% of false matches contain another bird. Literature: multi-label mixup is standard in BirdSet and BirdCLEF.

ladder.name: bg+overlap
ladder.change: The better of R1a / R1b, plus R2.
ladder.isolates: Do the two augmentations add up?
ladder.evidence: Depends on the R1 and R2 results.

ladder.name: pseudo-label
ladder.change: R3 plus a soft pseudo-label loss on unlabeled soundscape-train clips (one noisy-student round, teacher = pretrained).
ladder.isolates: What does supervision from unlabeled target audio add on top of augmentation?
ladder.evidence: Strongest external evidence (BirdCLEF noisy-student, Lasseck 2024), mostly competition write-ups. Risk: it can reinforce cross-species confusion.

ladder.name: best + anchored
ladder.change: The best configuration run with R0's anchored schedule. Only if R0 shows forgetting matters.

components.name: Background mixing (R1a, R1b, R3, R4)
params: Probability 0.5 per training clip (BirdSet's noise probability).
SNR drawn uniformly from −5 to 20 dB. The final range is set by Stage 2.1, so that the synthetic shift reproduces the real Δ_k.
Mixed on the waveform after the 5 s crop and before the gain augmentation: x' = x + g·b, with g chosen so that the power ratio of x to g·b equals the sampled SNR.
Labels do not change. Peak-normalise only if max |x'| > 1.
components.source: R1b backgrounds: soundscape-train clips in the lowest 30% of pretrained max species probability (a label-free quantile), random 5 s window. R1a backgrounds: generated coloured noise. One-off check of the selected clips against soundscape val labels, reported as a diagnostic and not used to tune anything.

components.name: Overlap mixing (R2, R3, R4)
params: Second clip: a random focal-train clip of a different species, random 5 s crop.
Relative level of the second clip drawn uniformly from −10 to 0 dB, so the primary species stays dominant.
Target = union of both labels. At most two sources.
components.source: Uses only focal labels, so it needs no soundscape labels.

components.name: Soft pseudo-labels (R4)
params: Teacher = pretrained model. Its sigmoid probabilities on unaugmented soundscape-train clips are computed once and cached.
Loss: soft binary cross-entropy on those probabilities with a small weight (0.2), plus the usual focal loss. Per step: 32 focal clips and 16 soundscape clips.
Soundscape clips get the existing masking and gain noise, not BG / OV mixing.
Push uses focal-train positives only, so pseudo-labels never place a prototype.
components.source: Round 1 only. Later rounds (student becomes teacher) only if round 1 helps. Monitor the fraction of top false matches that are other species.

evaluation.intro: Every model is scored by scripts/canonical_eval.py on the held-out test splits. The protocol is fixed; changing it means a new protocol version.
rows: Clips
Focal test (1,157) and soundscape test (3,600 clips, 30 sites). Identical for every model; the script refuses models evaluated on different clips.
Species
Primary: at least 30 soundscape test positives (7). Secondary: at least 5 in both test sets (12). Counts come from the test labels only, never from model output.
Headline
Soundscape macro AP on the primary species.
Secondary
Soundscape macro AUC (primary and 12), cmAP over the 12, and focal macro AUC / AP as a retention check (focal test is likely seen in pretraining).
Prototype level

Δ_k = soundscape AUC − focal AUC of each prototype's max activation as a detector of its species, for the 60 prototypes of the 12 species. Reported on all negatives (Δ) and on matched negatives (Δ birds). Counts of Δ < −0.10 and > +0.02, and the median.
Uncertainty

Cluster bootstrap with 1,000 resamples shared across models: whole sites for soundscape, whole recordists for focal. 95% percentile intervals. Unpaired intervals are wide because few sites carry the positives, so comparisons use paired differences.
Comparison
Paired differences against the baseline (pretrained) for every model, and the fraction of the baseline-to-oracle AP gap closed, each with a CI.
Success criteria
The four criteria below. Criterion 1 also requires the paired ΔAP interval to exclude zero.
How to run

Responses come from scripts/extract_prototype_activations.py (GPU) on the two test manifests. Then: python scripts/canonical_eval.py --model NAME responses.pt (repeat per model) --baseline pretrained-xcl --oracle soundscape-only. CPU only, about 75 s per model.
Not covered yet

Multi-seed aggregation (seeds are evaluated as separate models for now). Only the pretrained model has been scored under this protocol so far: the fine-tuned checkpoints live on filo and are not available here.

label_budget.intro: A diagnostic that separates a data gap from a methodology gap: how many labeled soundscape clips does it take to recover the gain? It also gives a yardstick for any label-free method (“equal to about N labeled clips”). It uses soundscape labels by design, so it is a reference experiment, not a candidate method.
rows: Question
How much of the pretrained-to-oracle AP gap does each labeled-clip budget close, and how many failing prototypes does it fix?
Budgets
Labeled soundscape-train clips: 0 (pretrained), 100, 250, 500, 1,000, 2,000 and all 7,200. The 7,200 point is rerun under the same fixed schedule, so the whole curve is comparable.
Sampling
Random clips from all 60 train sites, fixed seeds. A second variant draws whole sites instead (annotation is done on contiguous recordings in practice) once the first curve exists.
Schedule
The soundscape-only recipe (warm 2, joint 12, push, last 4). The number of optimizer steps is held constant by sampling with replacement, so only the amount of distinct data changes.
Selection
Fixed schedule, last epoch, no validation labels: in the few-label regime they would count against the budget.
Seeds
3 seeds (0, 1, 2) per budget. Report mean ± sd, plus the canonical paired CI for seed 0.
Readout
% of the AP gap closed and failing prototypes (Δ and Δ birds) against the number of labeled clips, and per primary species where positives allow. Label-free methods are placed on the same axis.
Interpretation
If a few hundred labels recover most of the gain, the gap is small in data terms and a label-free target is realistic. If it needs thousands, label-free methods face a much harder target.
Cost

16 runs (5 budgets × 3 seeds, plus the full rerun), each about as long as the earlier soundscape-only run (about 20 min), so roughly 5 GPU-hours, parallelizable. Constant steps mean small budgets save no time.
Code
scripts/train_protopnet.py: --train-labels N, a constant-steps sampler, and --select last (a few lines each). Evaluation reuses scripts/canonical_eval.py. No sbatch without approval.
